alignments.note: Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive; English writes no word for it (rules 23, 61).

Negative particle realized by the negative determiner *no*. The generic *man* is the subject the Greek infinitive leaves unexpressed and English must write, so it is a rule 7 helper on that infinitive under rule 74, exactly as this chapter puts *one* on γράφειν and *ye* on φιλοτιμεῖσθαι and περισσεύειν. Rules 41, 59 and 69 do not bear, no negative indefinite standing here, and rule 96's `οὐδεὶς θεός` → *there is no God* shows a bare *no* splitting from the noun it determines. Keeping *no man* whole on μή headed on *no* remains defensible.
Infinitive expanded into a finite clause: the supplied complementizer belongs to it (rule 85) and the supplied subject *man* is its helper (rule 74), discontinuous under rule 15.
Coordinating conjunction.
Second infinitive sharing the subject and negation already placed.
Genitive pronoun realized as the possessive *his*.
Head noun standing bare behind the possessive.
Article displaced by the genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ (rule 20).
Preposition realized by its own word.
Article surfaces as *the* (rule 19).
Head noun, split from its article under rule 13.
Causal conjunction.
Greek anarthrous; the supplied *the* is a rule 7/51 helper on the noun.
Verbless clause with a lexical noun subject: the supplied copula and determiner are the predicate nominal's helpers (rule 63).
Preposition realized by its own word (rule 36).
Quantifier.
Substantival demonstrative expanded with the generic *things*; head on the demonstrative (rule 17).
Comparative adverb; the answering καί has its own word *also*, so no *even* is supplied here (rule 82).
Particle realized by *also* (rule 65).
Finite verb with its English subject; the preverb sense is inside *forewarned* (rule 106).
Dative object rendered bare.
Coordinating conjunction.
Second finite verb sharing the subject.

review_notes: Corrected the *no man* unit: μή keeps only *no* and the supplied generic subject *man* moves to ὑπερβαίνειν under rule 74. No negative indefinite stands in this verse, so rules 41, 59 and 69 give μή no claim on a supplied noun, and rule 7's helper list does not cover a full lexical noun.

Everything else stands: s001 unrepresented under rule 61, s009 under rule 20, s013 taking the supplied copula under rule 63 because the subject κύριος is a lexical noun, and s018/s019 splitting *as* and *also* under rules 82 and 65.
Variant SBLGNT.1TH.4.6.v004 is underdetermined at s014; the projection's reading is aligned as it stands under rule 12.
